title: CHAPTER 5: CULTURE AND HERITAGE OF MADHYA PRADESH

blocks.content: UNESCO World Heritage Sites in MP
Other Important Archaeological and Historical Sites

items: Mandu (Mandav) - Medieval fort city, Malwa, famous for Jahaz Mahal and Baz Bahadur's Palace
Gwalior Fort - One of the greatest forts of India, Man Mandir Palace, Teli ka Mandir
Orchha - Bundela Rajput capital, Raj Mahal, Jahangir Mahal, Ram Raja Temple
Ujjain (Avantika) - One of 7 sacred cities, Mahakaleshwar temple, Kshipra River
Amarkantak - Source of Narmada and Son rivers, sacred site
Maheshwar - On Narmada, associated with Ahilyabai Holkar, Maheshwar Sarees
Vidisha (Besnagar) - Ancient city, Udayagiri caves, Heliodorus pillar (Garuda pillar)
Bhedaghat - Marble Rocks on Narmada, Dhuandhar Waterfall, Jabalpur
Deogarh (Tikamgarh) - Dashavatara Temple, Jain temples
Rai - Folk dance of Bundelkhand, performed by Bedia women, vigorous dance form with tabla accompaniment
Karma - Tribal dance of Gond, Baiga tribes (eastern MP) celebrating harvest and nature
Matki - Folk dance from Malwa region, performed by women
Badhai - Performed at festivals and marriages, associated with the Bhand community
Tertali - Folk dance from the Kamad community, women dance with cymbals attached to body
Grida - Tribal dance of Baiga tribe
Phulpati - Folk dance of Gond tribe
Lehangi - Folk dance from Bundelkhand region

blocks.content: Madhya Pradesh has a rich musical tradition. The Dhrupad style of classical music has strong roots in Gwalior, where Man Singh Tomar and Tansen's legacy is preserved. Tansen (Mian Tansen), one of the Navratnas of Akbar's court, was born in Gwalior and is considered the greatest musician in Indian history. The Gwalior Gharana is one of the oldest Khayal Gharanas in Hindustani classical music. The Tansen Samaroh (music festival) is held annually at Gwalior to honor Tansen's legacy.

Hindi is the official language of Madhya Pradesh. Several other languages and dialects are spoken in different parts of the state. Major dialects include Bundeli/Bundelkhandi (Bundelkhand), Bagheli/Baghelkhandi (Baghelkhand/eastern MP), Malvi/Malwi (Malwa), Nimadi (Nimar region on Narmada), Gondi and other tribal languages (eastern and central MP).

items: Hari Shankar Parsai - Pioneer of satirical Hindi literature, born in Hoshangabad
Gajanan Madhav Muktibodh - Hindi poet, associated with Nayi Kavita movement
Sharatchandra Chattopadhyay - Although Bengali, his works inspired many in MP
Ismat Chugtai - Urdu writer with connections to MP
Vishnu Prabhakar - Hindi writer, born in Muzaffarnagar but spent years in MP
Sharad Joshi - Famous Hindi satirist and humorist
Maheshwari Sarees - From Maheshwar (Khargone), handwoven silk-cotton sarees, patronized by Ahilyabai Holkar
Chanderi Sarees - From Chanderi (Ashoknagar), fine silk and cotton, GI tag
Bagh Print - Natural hand block printing from Bagh (Dhar), GI tag, done on Mahi River banks
Gond Paintings - Tribal paintings from Mandla, Dindori districts, famous artist Jangarh Singh Shyam
Pithora Paintings - Tribal paintings from Jhabua, Alirajpur (Bhilala tribe)
Batik Print - Indore region
Iron Craft - Bastar (border region)
Bamboo Craft - Tribal areas of eastern MP
Bell Metal Work - Balaghat and Seoni
